def test_post_boundary_activation_refusal_is_required(self):
        phases = self._phases()
        manager = {"before": self._snapshot(10, "i1", "boot-1"),
                   "after": self._snapshot(11, "i2", "boot-1"),
                   "after_phase": {"direct": {"rc": 0},
                                   "dependency": {"rc": 1}}}
        reboot = {"before": self._snapshot(11, "i2", "boot-1"),
                  "after": self._snapshot(12, "i3", "boot-2"),
                  "after_phase": {"direct": {"rc": 1},
                                  "dependency": {"rc": 0}},
                  "boot_id_before": "boot-1", "boot_id_after": "boot-2",
                  "qemu_pid_before": 99, "qemu_pid_after": 99,
                  "qemu_identity_verified": True}
        checks = vm.build_checks(phases, manager, reboot)
        self.assertFalse(checks["mask_persisted"])
evidence.reason: The test sets a successful activation after both boundaries (`manager.after_phase.direct.rc = 0` and `reboot.after_phase.dependency.rc = 0`) and only asserts `mask_persisted` is false. An implementation that checks only the manager boundary still sees the manager `rc=0`; one that checks only the reboot boundary still sees the reboot `rc=0`, so either partial implementation passes. Split into independent cases with all refusals valid except one boundary refusal changed to 0.
